*[[Whistler]]
*[[Zraii]]
</div><br clear="all">

==Behind the scenes==
===Genesis===
{{Quote|And then in 1995, out of the blue, I picked up the phone and there was Mike. It seemed he'd just been contracted to write a series of ''Star Wars X-Wing'' books for Bantam and wanted to discuss the Rogue Squadron group I'd created for my own ''Star Wars'' books.|Timothy Zahn|<ref name="X-Wing Omnibus 2" />}}
Rogue Squadron's origins date back to the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], which features Luke Skywalker commanding a team of snowspeeder pilots at the Battle of Hoth that he calls "Rogue Group."<ref name="ESB" /> The movie's [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] also designates them Rogue Group,<ref name="ESB novel" /> but its [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|radio drama]] identifies the pilots as "Rogue Flight,"<ref name="Radio Drama" /> a moniker that would be echoed in [[1984]]'s ''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]''.<ref name="A Guide to the Star Wars Universe Rogue Flight">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', published in [[1989]], uses the name Rogue Group, and it describes them as both "the brainchild of Luke Skywalker" and "a squadron of starfighter pilots who, in times of need, were pressed into service as snowspeeder pilots."<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3" /> ''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]'', released [[1990|one year later]], also calls them Rogue Group, and it states that Antilles took command of their remnants after Hoth and "formed them into the Rebel fleet's elite starfighter squadron."<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi 1st edition 41">''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>

It was author [[Timothy Zahn]] who coined the name "Rogue Squadron" in his [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'',<ref name="X-Wing Omnibus 2 Intro">Introduction to ''[[Star Wars Omnibus: X-Wing Rogue Squadron Volume 2]]''</ref> establishing the Rogues as an elite fighting force of the New Republic active<ref name="Heir to the Empire" /> five years after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="EC" /> According to Zahn, his first mention of Rogue Squadron was half a throwaway line and half convenience, as he wanted a unit that could be moved around wherever he needed it and thought that Wedge Antilles would be a good commander for such a unit.<ref name="Heir 20th Anniversary Edition chapter 9 footnotes">''[[Heir to the Empire: The 20th Anniversary Edition]]''</ref>

[[File:Battle-of-hoth-mcquarrie.jpg|thumb|left|325px|[[Ralph McQuarrie]]'s concept art of Rogue Group at the Battle of Hoth]]
The [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|second edition]] of ''Galaxy Guide 3'', published in [[1996]], updated its information to state that "Rogue Group" was born just after [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]{{'s}} Battle of Yavin, and that Antilles remodeled it and renamed it "Rogue Squadron" after the Battle of Hoth.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3 2nd Edition" /> ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' later set down a definitive timeline of the squadron's nomenclature: the unit formed after the Battle of Yavin was a small flight group called Rogue Flight, and when Hoth's Echo Base was attacked, Rogue Group was an ad hoc snowspeeder unit created from the pilots of Rogue Flight, Green Squadron, and Blue Squadron.<ref name="Warfare" /> The Rogues then became a full twelve-person squadron, Rogue Squadron, after Hoth's evacuation.<ref name="Shadows novel" /> This [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] only came in [[2012]], however, and most sources released before ''Warfare'' refer to the pre-Hoth Rogues as either Rogue Group or Rogue Squadron, instead of Rogue Flight.<ref name="Star Wars: Rogue Squadron" /><ref name="Galaxy Guide 3 2nd Edition" /><ref name="Rogue Squadron to the Rescue" /> Additionally, the comics [[X-Wing Rogue Squadron ½|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' ½]] and [[Empire 12|''Empire'' 12]], set just before the Battle of Yavin, erroneously identify the Alliance's Red Squadron pilots as Rogue Squadron.<ref name="X-Wing Rogue Squadron ½">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron ½|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' ½]]</ref><ref name="Empire 12">[[Empire 12|''Empire'' 12]]</ref>

A different origin story for the Rogues is given in [[Brian Wood]]'s [[2013]]&ndash;[[2014]] [[Star Wars (2013)|''Star Wars'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]] . The series' [[Star Wars (2013) 10|tenth issue]] sees Skywalker and Antilles flying in the Rebel Alliance's black ops [[Stealth Squadron]], which Antilles suggests renaming Rogue Squadron.<ref name="Star Wars 10">[[Star Wars (2013) 10|''Star Wars'' (2013) 10]]</ref> [[Star Wars (2013) 12|Two issues later]], he formally requests that Stealth Squadron be dissolved so that he may form Rogue Squadron, a proper Alliance squadron that fights out in the open. His request is approved.<ref name="Star Wars 12">[[Star Wars (2013) 12|''Star Wars'' (2013) 12]]</ref> This runs contrary to the Rogue Squadron origin story given in the second edition of ''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back''<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3 2nd Edition" /> and reiterated in such sources as ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''<ref name="CSWE Rogue Squadron" /> and ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="Warfare" /> The two conflicting stories have never been reconciled.

Several issues of [[Marvel Comics]]' [[1977]]&ndash;[[1986]] [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'']] series feature Rebel pilots flying X-wings in the time period between the battles of Hoth and Endor,<ref name="Coffin in the Clouds" /><ref name="Screams in the Void" /><ref name="Marvel Star Wars 100" /> and some of those pilots and their missions were later retconned into being a part of Rogue Squadron.<ref name="NEGTC" /><ref name="The Forgotten War" /><ref name="Fact File 111 Shira" /> At Endor, ''Return of the Jedi'' has Antilles flying as Red Leader rather than Rogue Leader,<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> which prompted 1990's ''Galaxy Guide 5'' to reveal that he renamed the Rogues before the battle as a tribute to the Red Squadron pilots who had fought bravely at Yavin.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi 1st edition 41" /> It was later confirmed that the name change was only temporary,<ref name="CSWE Red Squadron">{{CSWECite|III|88|Red Squadron}}</ref> with the [[1993]] novel ''[[The Truce at Bakura]]'' seeing them flying as Rogue Squadron again just one day after Endor.<ref name="Truce" />

===Development===
{{Quote|&hellip; because of your reaction to and reception of the novels. The way you embraced them and the characters opened a whole new realm within the GFFA. Before you latched on to the eclectic collection of pilots, ''Star Wars''™ was all princesses, pirates, droids and Jedi. Everyone else was expendable set dressing.|Michael A. Stackpole, thanking fans for the success of the ''X-Wing'' books|<ref name="Stormwolf interview">{{WebCite|url=http://www.michaelastackpole.com/?p=3567|text=Rogue One|author=[[Michael A. Stackpole]]|date=2015-03-13|work=Stormwolf|archivedate=20160115173321}}</ref>}}
Rogue Squadron was the focus of a multitude of works in the ''Star Wars'' [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]]. Author [[Michael A. Stackpole]] was contracted by [[Bantam Spectra]] in the mid-1990s<ref name="Stackpole TFN podcast 7-8 minutes">{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/podcast/story/Podcast_Michael_Stackpole_Interview_93830.asp|text=Podcast: Michael Stackpole Interview (Part 1)|date=2005-07-18|work=TheForce.Net|archivedate=20160106014516}}</ref> when they were considering buying a publishing license for the [[Star Wars video games|PC game]] [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']], and they ultimately purchased it and hired him to write four [[Star Wars: X-Wing (novel series)|''X-Wing'']] novels. [[Lucasfilm]]'s [[Sue Rostoni]] and author [[Kevin J. Anderson]] both urged him to use Wedge Antilles,<ref name="Echo Base Stackpole interview">{{WebCite|url=http://www.echostation.com/echo6/6stckpol.htm|text=Copy, Rogue Leader! Author Mike Stackpole leads Rogue Squadron on new missions|work=Echo Station|archivedate=20150906160421|partialdate=1996}}</ref> a fan-favorite hero from the [[original trilogy]],<ref name="Cult of Wedge">{{InsiderCite|23|Cult of Wedge}}</ref> as a main character, and Rostoni suggested that the first volume be about the Red Squadron pilots of ''A New Hope''. Stackpole decided that Rogue Squadron would be the ideal main focus, however,<ref name="Echo Base Stackpole interview" /> and he contacted Timothy Zahn to ask for details about the group in the [[New Republic era]].<ref name="X-Wing Omnibus 2 Intro" /> He logged a large number of hours playing the ''X-Wing'' and [[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''TIE Fighter'']] games in preparation for writing, and he also consulted real-life pilots, read pilots' biographies, and watched television documentaries on fighter squadrons, which were being prominently featured on television around the fiftieth anniversary of [[Wikipedia:Normandy landings|D-Day]].<ref name="Stackpole TFN podcast 15-17 minutes">{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/podcast/story/Podcast_Michael_Stackpole_Interview_93830.asp|text=Podcast: Michael Stackpole Interview (Part 1)|date=2005-07-18|work=TheForce.Net|archivedate=20160106014516}}</ref>

[[File:Stackpoleinthe90s.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Michael A. Stackpole penned numerous fan-favorite books and comics about Rogue Squadron in the 1990s.]]Stackpole has referred to the ''X-Wing'' books as "''[[Star Wars]]'' meets [[Wikipedia:Top Gun|''Top Gun'']],"<ref name="Insider 48 Bookshelf 75">{{InsiderCite|48|Bookshelf|''Star Wars'' Bookshelf}}</ref> which was in fact a theme suggested by Bantam editor [[Tom Dupree]].<ref name="The Adventures of Rogue Squadron 89">{{JournalCite|7|The Adventures of Rogue Squadron}}</ref> The novels proved to be massive hits, pleasing fans and reaching [[Wikipedia:The New York Times Best Seller list|''The New York Times'' Best Seller list]],<ref name="Stormwolf interview" /> and six additional volumes of the ''X-Wing'' series were later written, by Stackpole and by [[Aaron Allston]].<ref name="novels">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (novel series)|''X-Wing'' novels]]</ref> After being hired to write the novels, Stackpole was asked by Lucasfilm's [[Lucy Autrey Wilson]]<ref name="Echo Base Stackpole interview" /> in [[July]] [[1994]] if he had ever worked in comics. Not long afterward, [[Dark Horse Comics]] conceived of an ''X-Wing'' comic, and Lucasfilm told them to speak to Stackpole.<ref name="Horse's Mouth 34">{{InsiderCite|34|The Horse's Mouth|Straight from the Horse's Mouth}}</ref> Wilson helped him get hired to script the ongoing [[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'']] comic,<ref name="Echo Base Stackpole interview" /> which proved to be a long-running and much-loved series<ref name="Insider 48 Bookshelf 74">{{InsiderCite|48|Bookshelf|''Star Wars'' Bookshelf}}</ref> that, although canceled due to comparatively low sales, consistently remained one of Dark Horse's most requested titles for years.<ref name="Drawn By The Force Insider 83">{{InsiderCite|83|Drawn by the Force}}</ref> A number of the Rogues from the series were later immortalized as [[Hasbro]] 3¾ inch action figures.<ref name="Baron and Hobbie figures">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: 30th Anniversary Collection|packtype=''Star Wars'' Comic Pack|pack=#12: Baron Soontir Fel & Hobbie Klivian (''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' #24)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TACcomicpacks12.asp}}</ref><ref name="Ibtisam and Nrin figures">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Legacy Collection|packtype=''Star Wars'' Comic Pack|pack=Ibtisam & Nrin Vakil (''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' #19)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TLCcomicpacksWM091.asp}}</ref><ref name="Corran and Whistler figures">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Legacy Collection|packtype=Droid Factory Pack|pack=#5: Corran Horn & Whistler|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tlcDF05.asp}}</ref><ref name="Wedge and Borsk figures">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Legacy Collection|packtype=''Star Wars'' Comic Pack|pack=#14: Wedge Antilles & Borsk Fey'lya (''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' #32)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TLCcomicpacks14.asp}}</ref><ref name="Baron and Isard figures">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Legacy Collection|packtype=''Star Wars'' Comic Pack|pack=#17: Baron Soontir Fel & Ysanne Isard (''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' #29)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TLCcomicpacksLC17.asp}}</ref><ref name="Plourr and Dllr figures">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Legacy Collection|packtype=''Star Wars'' Comic Pack|pack=Plourr Ilo & Dllr Nep (''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' #13)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TLCcomicpacksWM103.asp}}</ref>

The squadron has featured in other ''Star Wars'' Legends works as well, such as the [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire|''Shadows of the Empire'']] multimedia project,<ref name="Shadows novel" /><ref name="Shadows comic 1" /> [[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|''The New Jedi Order'']] novel series,<ref name="Onslaught" /><ref name="Ruin" /><ref name="Rebirth" /> and the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' comics.<ref name="Legacy 41" /><ref name="Indomitable">''[[Star Wars: Legacy: Indomitable]]''</ref> They were also the focus of the six-part Rogue Squadron cycle of [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Card Game]]''.<ref name="Fantasy Flight Games Roque Squadron Cycle">{{FantasyFlightGames|url=en/news/2016/5/31/rogue-squadron-reporting-in|text=Rogue Squadron, Reporting In|date=2016-05-31}}</ref> A [[The X-Wing: Rogue Squadron Sourcebook|sourcebook]] about the squadron by [[Eric S. Trautmann]] was reportedly canceled following the closure of [[West End Games]],<ref name="Rogue Squadron Sourcebook Jedi Council Forums post">{{JCFCite|url=posts/3048776|board=Literature|thread=Star Wars: Lostworlds|user=genghis12|date=2001-06-13|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802105550/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/star-wars-lostworlds.2301212/page-5}}</ref> and author [[Andy Mangels]] once penned a Rogue Squadron comic called ''[[Boba Fett and X-Wing: The Mandalorian Candidate]]'' that was never published.<ref name="Andy Mangels TFN interview">{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/jedicouncil/interview/mangels.shtml|text=Andy Mangels|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20050301101325}}</ref> ''[[The Reenlistment of Baron Fel]]'', a story by Stackpole and Zahn about Soontir Fel leaving the Rogues and returning to Imperial service, was written as both a comic series and a four-part prose story, but neither version was ever sold.<ref name="Timothy Zahn TFN interview">{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/jedicouncil/interview/timothyzahn.asp|text=Interviews - Face To Face With The Masters|date=2008-10-29|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20190730061816}}</ref>

Three Rogue Squadron video games were developed by [[Factor 5]] and published by [[LucasArts]]. [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']] was released for the [[Wikipedia:Nintendo 64|Nintendo 64]] and [[Wikipedia:Personal computer|PC CD-ROM]] in [[1998]],<ref name="Star Wars: Rogue Squadron" /> and ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'' were respectively released in [[2001]] and [[2003]] for the [[Wikipedia:Nintendo GameCube|Nintendo GameCube]].<ref name="Rogue Squadron II" /><ref name="Rebel Strike" /> ''Rogue Leader'' was met with myriad critical acclaim<ref name="Rogue Leader Metacritic">{{WebCite|url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/gamecube/star-wars-rogue-leader-rogue-squadron-ii|text=Star Wars Rogue Leader: Rogue Squadron II|work=[[Wikipedia:Metacritic|Metacritic]]|archivedate=20180508153748}}</ref> and is still regarded as one of the best GameCube titles of all time.<ref name="Den of Geek Rogue Leader">{{WebCite|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/games/star-wars-rogue-squadron-space-combat-masterpiece|text=Star Wars: Rogue Squadron 2 – A Space Combat Masterpiece|author=John Saavedra|date=2019-11-09|work=[[Wikipedia:Den of Geek|Den of Geek]]|archivedate=20200311122531}}</ref><ref name="Nintendo Life Rogue Leader">{{WebCite|url=http://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/gamecube/star_wars_rogue_squadron_ii_rogue_leader|text=Star Wars Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader Review (GCN)|author=Martin Watts|date=2013-06-25|work=Nintendo Life|archivedate=20190201004735}}</ref> Factor 5 also developed a compilation of all three games, entitled [[Star Wars: Rogue Leaders: Rogue Squadron Wii|''Star Wars Rogue Squadron: Rogue Leaders'']],<ref name="IGN Rogue Leaders">{{WebCite|url=http://ca.ign.com/articles/2014/10/13/cancelled-star-wars-rogue-squadron-wii-game-footage-found|text=Canceled Star Wars Rogue Squadron Wii Game Footage Found|author=Jose Otero|date=2014-10-14|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|IGN]]|archivedate=20150725185349}}</ref> for the [[Wikipedia:Xbox|Xbox]], but the project was canceled by LucasArts. Further attempts to bring it to the Nintendo [[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]] were halted when Factor 5 went out of business. Another unfinished game, ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: X-Wing vs. Tie Fighter]]'', was also canceled and eventually became the [[2007]] [[Wikipedia:PlayStation 3|PlayStation 3]] game [[Wikipedia:Lair (video game)|''Lair'']].<ref name="Gamespot Rogue Leaders">{{GameSpot|url=articles/canceled-star-wars-rogue-squadron-game-details-eme/1100-6422908|text=Canceled Star Wars Rogue Squadron Game Details Emerge|author=Emanuel Maiberg|date=2014-10-12}}</ref>

In the ''Balance of Power'' expansion pack for the [[1997]] PC game ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing vs. TIE Fighter]]'', developed for LucasArts by [[Totally Games]], the player can fly as a Rogue Squadron pilot in Rebel missions against the Empire. A Rogue can also be the player character in the game's [[Balance of Power in the Airam Sector]] campaign, but the player can alternately choose to play that campaign and its battles on the side of the Empire.<ref name="Balance of Power" />

===Impact===
{{Quote|The Rogues are ace pilots with no shortage of derring-do, but they're also different from the heroes who normally take center stage in the ''Star Wars'' saga. Most aren't Force users destined to serve as fulcrums for the fate of the galaxy; rather, they're working-class heroes, loyal members of the military used to taking orders and performing difficult&mdash;or impossible&mdash;missions as best they can.|Jason Fry|<ref name="Who's Who" />}}
A [[2002]] ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' [[Who's Who in Rogue Squadron|article]] [[Star Wars Insider 59|written]] by [[Jason Fry]] asserted that "In the Expanded Universe of comics, books, and videogames, no military unit is more famous than Rogue Squadron." It also highlighted the Rogues' status as loyal, working-class heroes who follow orders and perform impossible missions, setting them apart from the Force-using movie heroes who often decide the fate of the galaxy.<ref name="Who's Who" /> Fans of Stackpole's ''X-Wing'' novels and comics agreed, telling the author that it was "very good to see someone else saving the [[Universe/Legends|universe]]."<ref name="Insider 48 Bookshelf 75" /> That analysis was echoed by [[Peet Janes]], who edited the ''X-Wing: Rogue Squadron'' comics and called the Rogues "some of the galaxy's greatest heroes, the 'working stiffs' of the ''Star Wars'' universe."<ref name="Horse's Mouth 34" /> On writing the [[2005]] comic miniseries [[Star Wars: X-Wing: Rogue Leader|''X-Wing: Rogue Leader'']], author [[W. Haden Blackman|Haden Blackman]] described Rogue Squadron as "a microcosm of the Rebel Alliance as a whole, composed of different people from different backgrounds all working together."<ref name="Drawn By The Force Insider 83" />

[[File:RogueSquadronNintendo.jpg|thumb|left|300px|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'', the first of three video games to star the Rogues]]
Writer Darren Franich of [[Entertainment Weekly Books|''Entertainment Weekly'']] opined that Stackpole's best contribution to the Rogues' saga "was to portray Rogue Squadron as the everymen-and-women of the Star Wars galaxy. They didn't fight zero-sum battles against Death Stars; they fought renegade Imperials and war lords, they fought on land and over sea, in space and beyond."<ref name="Entertainment Weekly Rogue One">{{WebCite|url=http://www.ew.com/article/2015/03/12/star-wars-spinoff-rogue-one-explained-brief-history-rogue-squadron|text='Rogue One' explained: A brief history of Rogue Squadron|author=Darren Franich|date=2015-03-12|work=[[Wikipedia:Entertainment Weekly|Entertainment Weekly]]|archivedate=20151017221518}}</ref> To Ryan Britt of [[Wikipedia:Tor Books|Tor.com]], the adventures of working-class pilots were both "something to see" and "endlessly interesting," and he suggested that the ''X-Wing'' comics were less like ''Top Gun'' in space and more akin to a mixture of [[Wikipedia:The A-Team|''The A-Team'']] and [[Wikipedia:Ghostbusters|''Ghostbusters'']].<ref name="tor.com">{{WebCite|url=http://www.tor.com/2014/05/01/working-class-star-wars-comics-were-something-to-see-rogue-squadron|text=Working Class Star Wars Comics Were Something to See: Rogue Squadron|author=Ryan Britt|date=2014-05-01|work=[[Wikipedia:Tor Books|Tor.com]]|archivedate=20160202060140}}</ref> While praising Stackpole's books, Andrew Liptak of [[Wikipedia:The Verge|''The Verge'']] expressed a belief that it was their popularity which proved ''Star Wars'' could exist without its [[Star Warriors (term)|figurehead characters]].<ref name="The Verge's Ode to Stackpole">{{WebCite|url=https://www.theverge.com/2016/12/18/13999686/x-wing-rogue-one-squadron-michael-stackpole-star-wars-books|text=An ode to Michael A. Stackpole's X-Wing series, Rogue One's spiritual ancestor|author=Andrew Liptak|date=2016-12-18|work=[[Wikipedia:The Verge|The Verge]]|archivedate=20190523080128}}</ref>

The name "Rogue Squadron" has been borrowed outside of ''Star Wars'' media, with a [[Wikipedia:Unmanned aerial vehicle|drone]] and counter-drone development team bearing the name launched in [[2017]] as part of the [[Wikipedia:Defense Innovation Unit|Defense Innovation Unit]] of the [[Wikipedia:United States Department of Defense|United States Department of Defense]]. In [[2020]], the unit transitioned to the DoD's Defense [[Wikipedia:United States Digital Service|Digital Service]],<ref name="Nextgov Rogue Squadron article">{{WebCite|url=https://www.nextgov.com/emerging-tech/2020/02/defense-digital-service-taking-over-drone-and-counter-drone-development-team/163074|text=Defense Digital Service is Taking Over a Drone and Counter-Drone Development Team|author=Brandi Vincent|date=2020-02-12|work=Nextgov|archivedate=20200814122733}}</ref> which had previously been involved in other projects with ''Star Wars''-inspired names, including a JEDI program, a Tatooine center, and a [[Jyn Erso|Jyn]] initiative.<ref name="Breaking Defense DDS article">{{WebCite|url=https://breakingdefense.com/2019/05/no-regrets-on-jedi-cloud-dds-chief-chris-lynch|text=No Regrets On JEDI Cloud: DDS Chief Chris Lynch|author=Sydney J. Freedberg Jr.|date=2019-05-01|work=Breaking Defense|archivedate=20200807224554}}</ref> The name "Rogue Leader" was also used by LucasArts for ''[[Rogue Leaders: The Story of LucasArts]]'', a [[2008]] book that chronicles the company's history.<ref name="Rogue Leaders sw.com article">{{SWArchive|url=vault/books/news20081203b.html|text=Recounting Rogues: ''Rogue Leaders'' Author, Rob Smith}}</ref>

In [[2015]], when the title of the rebooted ''Star Wars'' [[canon]]'s first [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology movie]] was revealed to be ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', the Rogues' adventures in ''Star Wars'' Legends received significant attention in online media among widespread speculation that the famous squadron would star in the [[2016]] film.<ref name="Entertainment Weekly Rogue One" /><ref name="Cinema Blend Rogue One">{{WebCite|url=http://www.cinemablend.com/new/5-Great-Rogue-Squadron-Stories-Use-Star-Wars-Rogue-One-70278.html|text=5 Great Rogue Squadron Stories To Use In Star Wars: Rogue One|author=Joseph Baxter|date=2015-03-12|work=Cinema Blend|archivedate=20150906012704}}</ref><ref name="The Guardian Rogue One">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theguardian.com/film/2015/mar/13/star-wars-film-episode-8-rogue-one-what-we-know|text=Star Wars Episode 8 and Rogue One: what we know|date=2015-03-13|work=[[Wikipedia:The Guardian|The Guardian]]|archivedate=20160104184630}}</ref> Although they ultimately did not,<ref name="Rogue One: A Star Wars Story">''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> a [[Rogue Squadron (film)|''Rogue Squadron'']] movie was later announced in [[2020]], with a projected release date of Christmas [[2023]].<ref name="They're actually doing it">{{SW|url=news/future-lucasfilm-projects-revealed|text=Future Lucasfilm Projects Revealed}}</ref> Director [[Patty Jenkins]] stated that it would include "great influence from the games and the books,"<ref name="IGN Great Influence">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/patty-jenkins-star-wars-rogue-squadron-movie-is-not-a-video-game-adaptation|text=Patty Jenkins' Rogue Squadron Movie Is Not a Video Game Adaptation|archivedate=20201212190041|author=Joshua Yehl|date=2020-12-12}}</ref> and she retweeted Michael A. Stackpole on [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] to thank him for his inspiring work.<ref name="Jenkins Thanks Stackpole on Twitter">{{Twitter|PattyJenks|status/1337189652478849024|[[Patty Jenkins]]|quote=I hope we make you proud. Thank you for your inspiring work. #RogueSquadron #StarWars @Lucasfilm_Ltd|archivedate=20201211001839}}</ref> She also told the [[Wikipedia:Associated Press|Associated Press]] that it was important to honor the history of the Rogue Squadron novels and video games, while still telling a new story in a new age.<ref name="Jenkins talks to the Associated Press">{{Twitter|APEntertainment|status/1410000613753069574|AP Entertainment|quote=Director Patty Jenkins (@PattyJenks) shares her vision for the next Star Wars film, "Rogue Squadron."|archivedate=20210629222206}}</ref> In late [[2022]], Jenkins revealed that she was unsure of the film's future,<ref name="Jenkins is unsure if the movie will happen">{{Twitter|PattyJenks|status/1602824242684252161|[[Patty Jenkins]]|archivedate=20221214013804}}</ref> and [[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] soon afterward claimed that according to their sources, the film was no longer in active development.<ref name="Variety says it's the end">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/star-wars-kevin-feige-patty-jenkins-movies-shelved-1235545774|text='Star Wars' Shakeup: Kevin Feige and Patty Jenkins Movies Shelved, Taika Waititi Looking to Star in His Own Film (EXCLUSIVE)|archivedate=20231125132422|author=Adam B. Vary|date=2023-03-07}}</ref> In [[April]] 2023, Lucasfilm President [[Kathleen Kennedy]] called the project "something that we still talk about, whether it's a movie, or whether it ends up being in the series space."<ref name="Kathleen Kennedy interview">{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@IGN|name=IGN|link=Wikipedia:IGN|video=qz6s7kvuwMc|text=Kathleen Kennedy on the Future of Star Wars Star Wars Celebration 2023}}</ref>

==Appearances==
